paper_type_rationale: The paper proposes a training-free inference-time algorithm for maintaining visual grounding during extended multimodal reasoning.
dominant_domain: Multimodal reasoning, test-time scaling, visual token reinjection, visually grounded reasoning.
must_cover: The core problem is visual token dilution during long text-heavy reasoning.
VisRef selects a compact visual token coreset at each reasoning step.
DPP scoring balances relevance to the current reasoning state and diversity over visual content.
An entropy-based stopping criterion controls overthinking and under-reasoning.
Main results show consistent gains over standard thinking and textual self-reflection across MathVista, MathVision, and MM-Star.
key_numbers: Main setting: entropy threshold 0.25, visual token budget 30% of total visual tokens, maximum steps 10.
InternVL3.5-8B gains over standard thinking: +5.4 on MathVision, +11.2 on MathVista, +5.9 on MM-Star.
SAIL-VL2-8B gains over standard thinking: +7.5 on MathVision, +5.1 on MathVista, +7.6 on MM-Star.
VisRef plus Look-Back reaches 83.1 on MathVista, 48.2 on MathVision, and 66.0 on MM-Star.
DPP objective reaches 79.3, 44.6, and 63.1, outperforming relevance-only selection.
Token budget from 20% to 30% improves MathVista accuracy from 76.1% to 79.2%; 40% plateaus.
Latency on MathVista with InternVL3.5-8B: standard thinking 7.1s, textual self-reflection 7.7s, Look-Back 7.6s, VisRef 8.2s.
Model scale appendix: InternVL-1B 52.0, InternVL-2B 58.1, InternVL-8B 79.3 with VisRef.
real_comparisons: Compared with standard thinking, VisRef reinjects visual token coresets during reasoning rather than relying on the initial image encoding only.
Compared with textual self-reflection, VisRef adds visual grounding rather than only extending text reasoning.
Compared with Look-Back, VisRef is training-free but can combine with the trained method for complementary gains.
Compared with ICoT and DaP-ICoT, VisRef operates at visual-token coreset level instead of inserting object images or image crops.

central_claims.claim: Long text-heavy multimodal reasoning suffers from visual token dilution, and visual reinjection can counteract it.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The paper shows that selective visual token reinjection improves performance and attention focus on the tested visual reasoning benchmarks.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove that every long multimodal reasoning failure is caused by visual dilution rather than planning or language reasoning errors.

central_claims.claim: DPP-based visual token selection is better than naive or single-term selection under a fixed budget.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: A relevance-diversity coreset gives stronger results than random or relevance-only selection in the authors' ablations.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not prove DPP is the only or globally optimal way to balance visual evidence diversity and relevance.

central_claims.claim: VisRef is a practical training-free test-time scaling method.
central_claims.what_it_actually_proves: The method is plug-and-play for the evaluated pretrained MLRMs and improves accuracy under fixed token budgets.
central_claims.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not eliminate latency overhead; the appendix reports extra inference cost from per-step DPP selection.

claim_boundaries: The main claims are scoped to MathVista, MathVision, MM-Star, and the listed MLRM backbones.
The method is training-free for model parameters, but it still changes decoding-time computation and context composition.
Efficiency is evaluated under token budgets and latency measurements, not as a zero-overhead improvement.
The entropy threshold and 30% token budget are tuned choices and may require adaptation in new settings.
negative_or_limiting_results: The limitations section explicitly states that DPP-based token selection adds inference latency.
Relevance-only selection is weaker than full DPP, showing that the method is sensitive to selection objective design.
Increasing the token budget beyond 30% does not improve accuracy, so more visual tokens can be wasteful.
Textual self-reflection can degrade performance on some visual-dependent settings, such as Qwen-3-VL-8B on MM-Star.
mechanism_result_map: Visual token reinjection maps to higher visual-to-text attention and better attention localization in qualitative figures.
DPP relevance-diversity scoring maps to Table 3 and Table 7 improvements over partial or random selection.
Entropy stopping maps to controlled reasoning length and the chosen threshold of 0.25.
Parallel visual-integrated traces under fixed budget map to Figure 3 test-time scaling gains over text-only parallel thinking.
comparative_positioning: VisRef is the visual-token-level counterpart to ICoT and DaP-ICoT, which work by inserting visual regions or object images.
VisRef is orthogonal to training-based Look-Back; combining the two yields the best Table 2 results.
VisRef differs from DeepScan because it does not discover new image regions through external visual experts; it reweights and reinjects existing visual tokens.
VisRef differs from PRCR because it focuses on coreset selection, while PRCR focuses on replay-free cache reuse and position rebinding.
reuse_takeaways: When testing visual reasoning systems, report whether longer text reasoning actually reduces visual attention.
Use a relevance-diversity selection objective when a fixed visual token budget forces compression.
Pair test-time scaling with an adaptive stopping rule to avoid uncontrolled overthinking.
For 3D agent work, adapt VisRef's gate to decide when to reinject rendered views or visual memory into a planning trace.
followup_questions: Would VisRef still help if the visual tokens come from multi-view 3D renders rather than a single 2D image?
How sensitive is DPP selection to the visual encoder and token granularity of each MLRM?
Can the entropy threshold be calibrated per model without validation labels?
Does visual reinjection help open-ended generation, or mainly closed-form answer benchmarks?
